newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Asian demand seen helping world gold market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Asian demand seen helping world gold market.

text.p: Renewed demand for gold in Asia is lending support to the international market after sagging late last year, consultant Gold Fields Mineral Services Ltd (GFMS) said on Wednesday.

"Physical demand did finally start to surge in January and for a time everyone was reporting shortages of 10-tola bars and even kilobars, with premiums rising accordingly," Stewart Murray of GFMS told the Australian Gold Conference.
Despite moving beyond the seasonally strongest part of the year, demand from Asian markets recently "suggests that they continue to provide a substantial floor," Murray said.
Still barring changes in investor sentiment, gold is forecast to trade in a familar price range for at least the next two years, Murray said.

"For the market to see a return of the long-lost bullion investor, there will have to be a change of investor sentiment on the question of official sector sales, or a catalyst such as a sign that equities and bond prices are ready to go into reverse," he said.

"Until this happens the gold price seems more likely to be determined by the fundamentals of physical supply and demand, with the price remaining in the trading range we have seen over the past year or two."
Whether gold trades high or low in that range is likely to depend on the decisions taken in treasury departments of gold producers and the offices of central bank governors, Murray added.
